It’s important to not prompt Theo to perform a cue that he is not ready to perform or has not practice under those circumstances. Remember, practice makes perfect. Practice all the suggested behaviors in different situations and environments where Theo is successful. Slowly practice outdoors as Theo’s confidence increases and starts to offer unprompted check-ins. Practice scenarios that you have experienced in the past without the distraction. Work on distance, distraction and duration as three separate levels of difficulty. See below a list of activities you can do to help Theo with his reactivity and also to meet strangers.Confidence:Sniffing GamesFind it! This is a great game to play encouraging your dog to find a treat (or toy if he has a favorite toy). Show your dog a treat or his favorite toy, and then place it out of his sight but easily accessible. Tell him to “Find it!”. Once he finds it praise enthusiastically. You can start to increase the difficulty of the game by turning off the lights, adding more treats, using boxes or even hiding treats in less conventional places like inside of a shoe. The rewards for the dog are multiple- he gets a treat or finds his toy plus a very happy handler. If issuing a toy, be sure to reward his find with some play before starting again. When multiple treats or toys are used, this particular game helps to build persistence and trust in the handler. The dog may initially find only 2 out of 3 treats, but he quickly discovers that persistence in searching when you give the “Find it!” cue pays off. He learns to believe you - there really is another one there! FreeworkIntroduction to FreeworkPlace snuffle mats and licky mats around an rea of your hours and load them with treats, yogurt, peanut butter, etc… Let your dog go in and explore the area while enjoying the amazing treats you set out for him. Don’t give him big pieces, this activity is more about the journey of finding the treats. Try using small crumbs so encourage more sniffing. You can also use your dog’s kibble for this. This game allows your dog to freely go in an area and explore. You can also do the same set-up outdoors to encourage him to sniff in situations where he might want to bark otherwise. Scatter FeedScatter Feeding Dogs: A Step-by-Step Guide To Our Favourite Calm Enrichment Activity!Why scatter feeding is beneficial for dogsScatter feeding provides a way for Theo to use his nose and calm down. You can use the same cue as “Find it!”. Do this in your back yard or even Sniffspots! Consent TestPetting Consent Tests movieParticing this form of consent testing will help Theo have some predictability when meeting strangers. Knowing that he wont be petted unless requested can be very empowering for dogs. When Theo meets strangers, please encourage your visitors to not do strong eye contact or talk to Theo at least initially. Let Theo do some freework or scatter feet for some minutes while he is adjusting to the presence of the new visitor. Communication:Teach Unprompted Attention/Auto Check-InAuto Check-In.pdfI am attaching a handout on how to do this but here is a short course on how to teach it with some demo videos: https://suzanneclothier.com/shop/autocheckin/This is very similar to the “Look at me” cue with the difference that it’s coming from the inside out where the dog is voluntarily offering attention. Puppy Politeness PokerPractice Puppy Politeness Poker by creating a list of reliable cues Theo will enthusiastically perform. Also create a list of real-life rewards that he will work for (meal time, access to a snuffle mat, opening a door, etc). Utilize those cues to give him explicit permission to access something he wants and change it up every time. This will teach Theo to slow down, listen to your request and work for what he wants. Teaches impulse control, attention and it polishes the communication between you and him. You can learn more about this concept by watching this free webinar: https://suzanneclothier.com/member_video_library/puppy-politeness-poker-webinar/Training:Teaching TouchTouch.pdfOnce Theo is able to give a “Touch” when cued in different situations, you can start using this cue during walks when you see that he spots an other dog and want to prevent him from reacting. You might need to use smellier rewards in the beginning. Practice WaitI don’t have a hand-out for wait but it sounds like Theo already knows this behavior and he just need to practice. Start small with baby steps. Take one step at a time to build distance. Once you are able to ask Theo to wait and go to a different room you can start working on duration. Once Theo is able to wait for a longer period of time you can throw in distractions like maybe closing a door and then opening it. The more you practice this, the easier it will be for him once you take it outside and introduce it in the stairs. Remember to start out with baby steps, even through Theo already has mastered “Wait” with distance, duration and distractions in-doors, you still want to start with just one step outdoors. Management:Teach 1-2-3 Treat! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ui6dWBDdDScI wasn’t able to find any great videos of this (I should make my own lol) but basically you condition your dog to expect a treat when they hear the word “three”. If you practice this in-doors with no distractions, you eventually will be abe to do this outdoors. When you see another dog coming then you can perform the pattern that Theo already knows and he will prefer to be next to you waiting for the treat instead of reacting to the other dog. Emergency “U” turnTeaching an Emergency U Turn Portland Dog Training/ Teach an Emergency U-Turn for your Reactive Dog/ Noble Woof Dog TrainingTeaching Theo an Emergency “U” turn will help you get out of situations where he is likely to react. By practicing this, you will be able to prevent him from practicing the undesirable behavior. Scatter FeedAfter Theo has had a lot of practice with the “Find it” cue, you can do a scatter feed during walks when you see there is a dog approaching on the opposite site of the street. Please be mindful that this would be done if you are sure that the other dog is not walking towards you or wont approach you. This is meant as a management technique to prevent him from reacting to an other dog and rehearse the undesirable behavior. TouchOnce Theo learns touch, you can also do this to basically step aside and call him over buy asking him to touch. This will allow you to position him an a way where he is not facing the other dog approaching and will buy you some time while the other dog finishes crossing. Follow up:I recommend booking an in-person appointment to work on counter conditioning and desensitizing Theo to other dogs during walks and address reactivity issues. Additionally we can work practicing polite greetings with strangers. To book your next in-person appointment please visit https://loyalpawrenting.pet/ → Book Now → First Let’s Meet → Step 2: In-Home Assessment.During this 1.5 hr visit, we will work on creating a customized training, enrichment and management plan to set up Theo for success. We will also perform a Relationship Assessment Test to determine behavior patterns in your relationship with Theo. If you are interested in self-paced training I recommend taking the following course by Victoria Stillwell: https://positively.com/learning/course/help-stop-reactivity

I observed that he was heavily panting due to stress. However, he would approach me with a wagging tail and allow me to pet his head and back. We left the mulch yard and went for a walk to the next yard over where he did a fence greeting with Bubba Boy. He seemed excited to meet another dog and I suspect he is dog friendly. We then walked inside and I brought him over to the supervisor desk. He stopped midway to greet two customers in which he offered submissive ears and a tail wag. Once at the desk, he was met by a few kennel techs. While he did show some shyness, he allowed one kennel tech to pet his head. We went back to 200, I placed him back in his kennel and unleashed without incident. Recommend L3-SF and a playgroup assessment.
